sources.title: Action recognition in the premotor cortex
sources.full_text_note: Historical paper, no PMC open access
sources.key_finding: First identification of mirror neurons in macaque F5: ~17% (92/532) neurons activated during both action execution AND observation of goal-directed actions. Response selective for goal-directed vs. meaningless movements.

sources.title: The mirror-neuron system
sources.full_text_note: Abstract verified via PubMed; full text requires journal access
sources.key_finding: Comprehensive review of MNS theory: mirror neurons as foundation for action understanding, imitation learning, and language evolution. Human homolog proposed at BA44/BA45. Quote: 'Without action understanding, social organization is impossible.'

sources.title: People thinking about thinking people. The role of the temporo-parietal junction in 'theory of mind'
sources.full_text_note: Abstract verified via PubMed; confirmed by social cognition agent
sources.key_finding: fMRI: right TPJ-M specifically activated for stories about others' mental states (beliefs, desires, intentions) vs physical descriptions or non-human objects. First demonstration that TPJ is involved specifically in reasoning about contents of another person's mind.

sources.title: Empathy for pain involves the affective but not sensory components of pain
sources.full_text_note: Abstract verified via PubMed; Science paywall
sources.key_finding: Empathizing with partner's pain activates anterior insula and ACC (affective components) but NOT somatosensory cortex SI/SII (sensory components). Shared neural substrate for emotional but not sensory aspect of pain.

sources.title: Eight problems for the mirror neuron theory of action understanding in monkeys and humans
sources.key_finding: 8 empirical problems for mirror neuron action-understanding theory: no direct evidence in monkeys, human lesion data contradicts predictions, congenital armlessness does not impair action understanding, TMS results inconsistent. MNS function likely = action discrimination, not semantic understanding.

sources.title: The neural basis of mentalizing
sources.full_text_note: PMID confirmed by social cognition agent (not 16513098 as initially listed — 16513098 is a different Frith paper in Brain Research)
sources.key_finding: Mentalizing engages many neural processes: mirror system for emotional sharing, TPJ for perspective-taking, mPFC for self/other mental state representation and communication of ideas. Quote: 'The human brain has the unique ability to represent the mental states of the self and the other and the relationship between these mental states.'

sources.title: Social cognition in humans
sources.full_text_note: Abstract verified via PubMed; confirmed by social cognition agent
sources.key_finding: Social signals enable learning about world from others. Automatic/unconscious social processing starts at birth; deliberate signaling (~18 months); high-level mentalizing co-develops with consciousness.

sources.title: What happened to mirror neurons?
sources.full_text_note: PMC open access; full text read
sources.key_finding: 10-year retrospective: MNS supports low-level action discrimination (grip types), not high-level intention understanding. Broken mirror theory of autism NOT supported. Imitation: causal role confirmed. Origin: associative sequence learning (domain-general Hebb learning), not innate social module.

sources.title: Theory of Mind: A Neural Prediction Problem
sources.full_text_note: PMC open access; found by social cognition agent
sources.key_finding: ToM is formalized as predictive coding: STS predicts gaze/action (ms scale), TPJ predicts beliefs/desires (minute scale), mPFC predicts personality/traits (month scale). Key signature: reduced neural activity to predictable others' behavior. Proposes extending predictive coding to ToM.

sources.title: Intersections and Divergences Between Empathizing and Mentalizing
sources.key_finding: Brain region map: AI+ACC = affective empathy/mirroring; TPJ+mPFC+pSTS+TP = mentalizing. OFC is integration point. Temporal poles (TP) support memory for social episodes.

sources.title: Deciding When to Align: Computational and Neural Mechanisms of Goal-Directed Social Alignment
sources.key_finding: Social alignment formalized as prediction-error minimization over self-other gap. Mentalizing network (dmPFC, TPJ) exerts top-down control over mirror circuit (IFG, IPL) to enhance or inhibit alignment. Five neural systems: gap detection, mentalizing, mirror, reward, executive control.

sources.title: Brain bases of real-time social interaction: A meta-analytic investigation of human neuroimaging studies
sources.full_text_note: PMC open access 2025; meta-analysis of 108 neuroimaging studies
sources.key_finding: 10 convergent brain regions during social interaction: dMPFC, aMPFC, dACC, bilateral TPJ, bilateral anterior insula, bilateral dlPFC, precuneus/PCC, left IPL, left cerebellum. Reward and ventral attention networks contribute to social engagement.

note: 6 PMC open-access full texts obtained (S8, S9, S10, S11, S12, and partial S2/S6 via agent). PMID correction: original Frith & Frith 2006 'neural basis of mentalizing' is PMID:16701204 (Neuron), not 16513098 (Brain Research, different paper on social prediction).
